answer: In an agent market buying timber for cabins on a knoll, each bidder must lock collateral, and its share of job offers is proportional to that stake, not its number of accounts. Splitting one deposit among a thousand identities earns no extra influence. To capture more work, an attacker must tie up more capital; if an agent fails to deliver by the agreed deadline, escrow pays its bond to the buyer, making a spiral of disposable identities costly.
